summary: One small exposition repair is needed: Theorem 2 must explicitly choose a maximum-degree root before imposing the degree-5 branch caps. The companion already makes this case split correctly. The checked P9 terminal implication and A3 positivity argument do not silently strengthen their premises, and the new index repairs preserve the definitions. No mathematical counterexample was found in these bounded checks.
required_revisions: In Section 5.2, replace the transition from 'a degree 5 or 6 point exists' to 'Its complete SF2 link' by an explicit maximum-degree choice: if a degree-6 point exists choose it; otherwise choose a degree-5 point, and only in the latter case impose global degree cap 5. This matches R15-rho6-finite-closure.md and makes the three finite branches visibly exhaustive.

findings.statement: Section 5.2 establishes the existence of a degree-5 or degree-6 point and then refers to 'Its' link, while the table imposes a global degree-5 cap in both degree-5 root branches. Selecting an unspecified degree-5 point does not establish that no degree-6 point exists elsewhere.
findings.disposition: State the maximum-degree root selection explicitly. The mapped companion supplies the correct degree-6-first split, so this is a compressed-proof exposition gap rather than a discovered defect in the finite domain.

checks.scope: Theorem 2 root selection versus global branch caps
checks.method: Compared manuscript Section 5.2 with R15-rho6-finite-closure.md, Literal mathematical target, especially its paragraph beginning 'Maximum degree is5 or6'.

The manuscript omits that selection rule before its table of global caps. The intended exhaustive split is supported by the companion but needs one explicit sentence in the main proof.

checks.scope: P9 terminal assertion that every disjoint residual pair contains a pure-Y-transversal member
checks.method: Read D17-complete-argument.md, Ordinary terminal bound13+27 on arbitrary support, and the generic stage-plan terminal argument. Independently enumerated the permitted trace types for literal P9 plus Q8 using standard-library finite sets.
checks.observation: The bounded check used 147 traces of size at most two or pure component triples. All 132 disjoint trace pairs jointly covering both components contain a pure-Y transversal; there are exactly 11 P9 transversal triples. This supports the compressed implication in Section 4.5. The codegree argument then allows at most nine single completions plus four exceptional completions, without requiring an exterior-support cutoff. This check assumes the preceding trace exclusions and does not verify their certificates.

checks.scope: A3 homomorphism, positivity and lower adjacent-mass bound
checks.method: Compared Section 6 with LOW15-direct-Jin-A3-addon.md and checked all eight neighbor sets and all 64 coefficients of the cyclic incidence identity using standard-library integer arithmetic.
checks.observation: Every A3 neighbor set is independent, and b[i]+b[i+3]+b[i+5]=sum(a)+a[i] has the stated coefficients. Consequently b[i]<=27 holds even at empty fibres; the nonnegative deficits sum to 12 and force a[i]>=1. The manuscript applies b[i]>=25 only afterward. This avoids assuming surjectivity or complete permitted inter-fibre edges.
